tasks.task: Establish site, isolate balconies, brief occupants
tasks.scope: Set up compound in courtyard and Kiora Lane, establish occupant liaison protocol, issue work notices, establish exclusion zones below active balconies.
hazards: trip hazard — uneven courtyard surface, temporary barriers, cable runs
struck by falling object — work at height above unaware pedestrians in courtyard
occupant confusion or non-compliance — incomplete or delayed hazard communication
tasks.dominant_hazard: struck by falling object — work at height above pedestrians in courtyard
controls: Establish exclusion zone minimum 3 m radius below each active balcony work area — barricade with high-visibility mesh and post warning signs at all pedestrian entry points.
Brief all occupants via written notice 7 days before work starts — state work hours, noise levels, access restrictions, and emergency contact.
Conduct site induction with all workers and occupants present — confirm understanding of exclusion zones, fall hazards, and stop-work triggers.
Position spotters at courtyard entry points during all elevated work — spotters must prevent occupant entry and signal work suspension if persons approach exclusion zone.
Install edge protection (guardrail or netting) at all active balcony perimeters before elevated work — verify 1.1 m height minimum and secure against wind.
Mark cable runs and scaffold base footprint with high-visibility tape — remove trip hazards or provide ramps where cables cross pedestrian routes.
Confirm EPA licence on site and visible at all entry points — provide copy to occupants on request.
Hold daily occupant liaison briefing at 07:30 — confirm ongoing compliance, address concerns, record attendance.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: EPA licence is on display and scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and received by site supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant or unauthorised person breaches exclusion zone during elevated activity.
🛑 STOP WORK if: spotter is absent or unable to maintain line of sight to active work area.
🛑 STOP WORK if: weather conditions prevent clear visibility or wind speed exceeds state for edge protection.

collapse or instability — inadequate bracing, substrate failure, overload during erection
struck by scaffold component — dropped parts during assembly, swinging loads

check substrate (concrete balconies, roof penetrations, fixings) for cracks, spalling, or load capacity limits before installing base plates or standards.

Assign spotter to monitor exclusion zone below balcony during debris removal — stop work immediately if occupied zone is breached.
Check edge protection, guardrails, and toe boards on scaffold before each shift — confirm handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder.
Collect all tile and screed debris in sealed rigid containers — do not allow debris to accumulate on balcony surface or drop uncontrolled.

🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection, guardrail, or scaffold platform becomes damaged, loose, or unstable during work.

tasks.task: Apply new waterproofing membrane system
tasks.scope: Clean and prime prepared slab. Apply liquid or sheet membrane system per product technical data. Cover all areas including details, penetrations, and edges.
hazards: inhalation of solvent vapour or isocyanate fume — liquid membrane primer and resin application in confined courtyard air
skin or eye burn — contact with reactive membrane components or primer
fire or explosion — flammable solvent vapour in proximity to ignition source or hot work nearby
fall from height — operative on balcony edge applying membrane, slip on wet primer or membrane
tasks.dominant_hazard: inhalation of solvent vapour or isocyanate fume — liquid membrane application in occupied building
controls: Obtain and review product SDS on point of use before any membrane or primer application starts.
Verify substrate is clean, dry, and primed per product technical data — sign off in site diary before membrane application.
Establish forced mechanical ventilation across work area — air movement must travel away from occupied zones and exhaust outside building.
Prohibit hot work, ignition sources, and smoking within 10 m of application area while solvent vapour is present.
Wear half-mask respirator with organic vapour and particulate cartridges — fit check and seal before each shift.
Wear chemical-resistant chemical-resistant gloves and full-length sleeves — check gloves for puncture or tear before each use.
Wear eye protection— change immediately if splashed or fogged.
Establish exclusion zone below and around elevated work — barricade or delineate to prevent public access during and 2 hours post-application.

struck by tile or tool — dropped tile or trowel from balcony onto occupied courtyard below

tasks.task: Clean balconies and reinstate occupant access
tasks.scope: Remove work debris, wash down balconies, remove temporary signage. Reinstate balconies for occupant use. Remove exclusion zones and restore courtyard and Kiora Lane.
hazards: slip hazard — wet balcony surface, spilled water or cleaning compound during washdown
struck by debris — dislodged tile, sealant, or temporary signage during removal or washdown
occupant re-entry confusion — inadequate notice of access reinstatement, occupants enter work zone prematurely
tasks.dominant_hazard: slip hazard — wet balcony surface during washdown and cleaning
controls: Apply non-slip matting or anti-slip tape to all wet balcony surfaces before washdown starts.
Erect temporary 'Wet Floor' signs at balcony entries and stairways. Remove only after surface dries.
Use low-pressure wash (not high-pressure jet) to avoid dislodging tiles, sealant, or temporary fixings.
Collect and contain all washdown water and cleaning compound runoff using bunds or drain covers.
Brief occupants in writing 48 hours before reinstatement — specify date, time, access routes, and post-work condition.
Remove all temporary signage, barriers, and exclusion tape only after final washdown dry-down is complete.
